The location was hard-coded in ten places (action_admission, vigilia/continuity, prompt_sources, claude-workflow-guard, claude-usage, capture-session-claim, codex-claude-daily-review, corpus-feed, agent-session-full-stack-review, session_sources); all went blind at once and NOTHING went red. Measured fault at discovery: ExitPlanMode failed 15/37 = 41% (Fable 14 fail/10 ok vs Opus 1 fail/13 ok), absorbing (8 consecutive failures over 2h07m; re-entering plan mode did not clear it).
action: Executable predicate wins over a literal. (1) The dependency is DECLARED: LIMEN_CLAUDE_HARNESS_ROOT in institutio/governance/parameters.yaml. (2) It is RESOLVED in exactly one place: cli/src/limen/harness_paths.py — env override -> <repo>/.agent-runtime/claude -> the shared checkout's copy when running in a worktree -> ~/.claude, with is_session_path() matching harness layout by shape so the carve-out holds under an arbitrary cwd. (3) It is SENSED: scripts/harness-root-probe.py + the harness-root-probe beat sensor assert root liveness (empty-while-a-sibling-is-full = relocated) and scan three structural plan-mode signatures (A exit rejected, B mutation while mode=plan excluding the session's own plan file, C one plan slug written to both a shared and a worktree path). Signatures match on JSON structure, never on error text — substring matching also catches sessions merely discussing the error (3 false positives when prototyped). Regression test: cli/tests/test_codex_host_admission_hook.py::test_repo_local_harness_root_is_admitted. Generalized as IF-HARNESS-SENSED. Two residual defects are inside the Claude Code binary and are worked around, not fixed here: toolPermissionContext.mode desyncing from the session permissionMode (and not resyncing on re-entry), and EnterPlanMode being shouldDefer:true so the error's own recovery advice can never execute (0 invocations across 258 transcripts).

subject: scripts/diurnal.py shipped has_body() as `(root/'logs'/'.voice').is_dir()`, documented "True iff this root is a live organism, not a bare projection", guarding what its own sibling docstring called "the single most dangerous failure mode this organ has". It exited 0 and wrote the page. The stamp it trusted is written by beat-sensors.py, which resolved its own root the same way — so a sensor running in a worktree MANUFACTURED the body that fooled the guard.
action: standing rule: a liveness guard that a SINGLE WRITE can satisfy is not a liveness guard. Presence of a directory, of a file, of one stamp, is evidence that something once ran — never that this is the living thing. Prefer an EXACT structural discriminator over a heuristic one where any exists (a linked worktree's .git is a gitdir-pointer FILE; a checkout's is a DIRECTORY — already implemented correctly four times in this repo and never packaged until scripts/_root.py). Where only a heuristic exists, require a population floor, not existence. Corollary, and the reason this class is dangerous rather than merely wrong: a hollowed-out report reads CALMER than a correct one, so the failure presents as good news. Fix at the SOURCE (stop the sensor stamping a worktree) rather than teaching every reader to distrust the signal — ~13 organs read logs/.voice as ground truth.

subject: A safety guard degrades silently toward 'everything is fine' whenever its input is stale, unresolvable, undeployed, or unarmed - because 'I could not resolve this' and 'this is fine' are encoded as the same value. Measured four times in one stack on 2026-08-07: model_selection._fable_balance / fable-session-guard._load_balance / vendor-cancel-advisor._fable_over_cap all returned `dict | None`, and None meant both 'no meter' and 'a meter I decided not to trust', with every caller reading it as permissive; fable-session-guard._resolve_model returned '' for an unresolvable session model, so _is_fable('') was False and the guard exited 0 printing zero bytes - byte-identical to a confirmed-cheap session; an undeployed copy of a guard printed superseded advice with no indication it was pre-merge; and an unarmed SessionStart hook was indistinguishable from one that ran and found nothing. The incident: the live checkout sat 36 commits behind origin/main, so the deployed fable-allotment.py scanned a directory holding 0 transcripts and rewrote logs/fable-allotment.json to spent_pct 0.0 / over_cap false EVERY BEAT while the true figure was 75.47% / over_cap true - releasing both Fable brakes and burning ~50% of a weekly allotment in two days with no downgrade and no warning. THE LOAD-BEARING DETAIL: the meter file was FRESH and WRONG (rewritten 09:17 that morning and every beat before it), so any age bound on the artifact PASSES on this incident. Freshness of an artifact is not truth of its value when the stale party is the writer's code.
action: standing rule: a guard that cannot establish its input must WARN, never pass. Three bindings. (1) NEVER type a trust-bearing read `dict | None` - that type has no room for 'unknown', so unknown collapses into permissive; return an explicit verdict {state, trusted, detail} where every failure mode is a distinct named state. (2) An unresolvable input costs a TIER, never the WORK: withhold the reserved capability and let the job proceed at the next rung down, so degrading is always affordable and never has to be switched off. (3) A hatch is POLICY, not truth - implement it in the CONSUMER (an `enforced` flag), never by making the reader lie about what it saw; and never add a second, broader quiet switch, which re-creates the defect as a supported feature. Corollary for detection: this class is chronic and every prior episode produced a NEW SENSOR, all of them severity:advisory - IF-LIVE-TREE-COHERENCE (six days on a tree where three subsystems did not exist), sensors.yaml beat-freshness (seven flywheel PRs inert 18h; a 15-day starvation on the same unrun restart atom), sync-release.sh (60 behind for three days 'of loud fail-open beats'). Detection is complete and has no teeth. Do not answer a recurrence with another advisory sensor; give an existing one a consumer that pays a price. This is PREC-2026-07-08-armed-valve-outcome one domain over: a beat-wired organ running in permanent dry-run is an UNMET outcome, not a filed one.

subject: A proof-by-execution harness proves exactly what its DECLARED population says, so a reader with two resolvable inputs whose declared degenerate cases all vary ONE input leaves the other axis unproven while the gate prints OK. Measured on the cadence-guard arc's own shipped tree: limen.model_selection:opening_verdict(pin, ceiling) had three declared degenerate cases in parameters.yaml and all three passed only args[0], the pin. The ceiling axis was never enrolled, so opening_verdict('claude-haiku-4-5', 'banana') returned {'state':'ok','trusted':True,'ceiling':'haiku'} - a degenerate input returning TRUSTED, the one outcome guard_contract forbids - while check-guard-degradation.py exited 0 reporting '3 degenerate case(s) all degrade toward the warning'. It survived a seven-fix arc explicitly built to close this class because the defect INVERTS BY INPUT: an unresolvable ceiling collapses to the cheapest rung, so every pin dearer than the cheapest returned above-ceiling (fail-toward-caution, no incident, nothing to force it up) and only the cheapest pin returned trusted. A defect that fails safe in the common case generates no evidence of itself. The same collapse was reachable by capitalisation alone (LIMEN_CLAUDE_SESSION_OPEN_MAX_TIER=Opus -> 'haiku'), because the pin was lowercased on its way in and the ceiling was not.
action: standing rule: a declared degenerate population is scoped to the READER, never to one of its arguments. Four bindings. (1) When declaring guard_state.degenerate for a reader of arity > 1, declare at least one case per resolvable input; a population that varies one argument proves one argument. (2) Choose the case's OTHER arguments to be the ones that make the defect visible - here the CHEAPEST pin, the only value that returned trusted; a case built from a typical value would have passed against the broken code and certified the bug. (3) Before trusting a fix that 'already landed', re-run the invariant against the shipped tree: _cap_rung's docstring names the cheapest-on-unknown substitution as 'this arc's own defect wearing a different hat' while still returning ladder[0] - it generalized the LADDER, not the unclassifiable value, and the prose read as a closure it never made. (4) Normalize a DECLARATION (case, whitespace) before judging it unresolvable, and normalize it wherever the value is read, not at one accessor: 'the cap belongs to the VALUE, not one accessor' was written in D6 and honoured only for the hard cap.

subject: An automated reviewer that re-reviews EACH NEW HEAD is a generator, not a gate, so an agent that treats its findings as blocking enters a loop with no fixed point. Measured on organvm/limen#2122 (fix/notification-routing-truth-2120): 4 days (first commit 2026-08-08T15:40, last 2026-08-12T19:22), ~180 commits, +5838/-204 across 29 files, and 167 inline review comments of which 119 came from a single bot (chatgpt-codex-connector), 23 coderabbitai, 3 Copilot. Comparable PRs in the same window drew 0, 6, and 0. The loop diverges rather than converges because every fix ADDS lines, enlarging the surface the next round reviews; the degenerate tail is visible in the log as 'style(test): restore terminal newline' three consecutive times at 2026-08-09T00:35 and 'style: normalize top-level spacing' twice - commits repairing churn caused by the previous commit. The decisive fact is that NONE of it was ever a gate: scripts/merge-policy.sh 2122 returned CLEARED (non-deploy, mergeState CLEAN, 12 checks, 0 failing, 0 pending) and the charter already states that an advisory check never holds a non-deploy merge. The agent invented a blocking obligation the repo's own predicate refuses to impose, then served it for four days. The last bot comment landed at 22:30Z - AFTER the agent stopped - proving round 8 was already queued and only the operator's interrupt ended it. The self-report was also stale in the safe direction: the session closed claiming 'the remote pr-gate had not finished', when it had finished green.
action: standing rule: an automated reviewer is a GENERATOR, not a gate. Three bindings. (1) The merge decision belongs to scripts/merge-policy.sh alone - when it exits 0 CLEARED, merge; residual reviewer findings become follow-up issues, never a pre-merge obligation. (2) Bound any fix-on-review cycle at N rounds (default 2) and stop with a loud verdict naming the unaddressed findings; a third round is evidence the reviewer is generating, not converging. (3) A revision loop is the twin of the endless-watcher ban of 2026-07-15 - both unbounded, both silent, both outliving their purpose - so it takes the same remedy: hard cap plus terminal verdict. Encoded in CLAUDE.md -> Merge & Branch Protocol beside that ban.

subject: A custody/backup predicate that asserts the MECHANISM moved, rather than the CONTENT being covered, reports green over an uncovered estate — and the gap is structurally unobservable, because the mechanism keeps moving for whatever it CAN carry. Measured on scripts/arca-freshness.py: its predicate was 'the vault remote was pushed within --max-age-days (2) AND a local working copy exists'. Both held while (a) _health-, _life- and _people-private all carried unsealed changes, including the session review artifacts that prompted the check, and (b) _collaboration-operations-private (4.9GB) had NEVER been sealed once since its creation on 2026-08-02 — it exceeds ARCA_MAX_MB=512, so seal_store skipped it on every beat and it had no off-machine copy of any kind, HORREVM custody being PARKED on L-CLOUD-EGRESS-CONSENT. The vault kept being pushed for the OTHER stores, so recency stayed green over a store it had never once carried. arca.sh cmd_status already COMPUTED the true answer via store_hash and discarded it as display text with exit 0, so nothing could consume it; the skip's only alarm was a log line in a 21MB heartbeat log that no predicate reads. Two amplifiers made the silence durable: the SEALER (arca.sh backup) lives in metabolize.sh 5c and the heartbeat daemon never runs metabolize (only saturate.sh does, heartbeat-loop.sh:590), so the effector ran far more rarely than the observer; and the observer's own regression fixture was a time bomb — FAKE_GH_PUSHEDAT was a value but was cat-ed as a path, so every run fell through to a hardcoded 2026-08-08 literal, green near that date and permanently stale once the clock passed the threshold. This is the same defect class the script's own docstring was written to close (an 8-day silent vault, #2072), reappearing one level up: the fix asserted that the vault was alive, not that it held anything.
action: standing rule: a custody predicate must assert COVERAGE, not liveness. Four bindings. (1) For any backup/mirror/sync gate, ask 'does the target hold what the source has NOW?' — never 'did the target change recently?'. Recency answers whether the mechanism is alive; only coverage answers whether it took what changed. (2) A skip, cap, or exclusion inside an effector must raise a PREDICATE, never a log line; 'a silent skip would read as covered, so this line is the alarm' is only true if something reads the line, and in a 21MB beat log nothing does. (3) When an effector and its observer run on different cadences, the coverage truth belongs in the OBSERVER — it is the half that looks often. (4) Behavioural corollary, and the reason this was found at all: never hand the operator a question a registry already owns. The trigger was a closeout that told him a review under ~/Workspace/_people-private/ was 'on this disk only — tell me where it should live', when his-hand-levers.json → L-ARCA-KEY-ESCROW states verbatim that ARCA seals every ~/Workspace/_*-private store into the private vault. The claim felt true only because of the defect above; the correct move on any 'is this durable?' question is to RUN the custody predicate, never to infer from the absence of a .git directory and never to route the question back to him.

subject: Local clones of satellite product repos vanish from disk without ceremony, and a workflow that treats the clone as the artifact loses nothing only by luck. Measured twice in 24h on the dustin venture repos: (1) 2026-08-12 — /Users/4jp/Workspace/post-dsp-platform disappeared AFTER a successful push (verified by a fresh clone running its full 59-test suite green); the same session had also watched `gh repo clone` print 'Cloning into...', exit 0, and create NOTHING (the directory existed only because a Write tool call later created a file in it — git status then said 'not a git repository'). (2) 2026-08-13 — ALL THREE venture clones (post-dsp-platform, the-consulate, new-ancients-social) were absent at session start; a depth-5 find over /Users/4jp plus a full ls of ~/Workspace confirmed a firm negative, while the GitHub copies were intact at the pushed heads. The failure shape is silent in both directions: a clone that exits 0 having created nothing, and a directory that is gone after the work was pushed.
action: standing rule: GitHub is the copy of record for satellite product repos; the clone is a cache. Three bindings. (1) Before the first commit in any fresh clone, verify it is real: `git -C <dir> rev-parse --show-toplevel` — never trust `gh repo clone`'s exit 0 or the directory's existence. (2) Before EVERY write stage in a multi-stage run, re-probe `git -C <abs> rev-parse HEAD` against `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits/<branch> --jq .sha`; divergence or absence means re-clone before proceeding, never write into an unverified tree. (3) Push after every logical unit — the vanish costs nothing precisely when everything of value is already on the remote, and a fresh clone running the pushed test suite is a STRONGER verification than trusting the local copy. The dustin closeout predicate encodes (2) as its first per-repo check (scripts/dustin-alpha-omega-done.sh).
authorised_by: sessions 2026-08-12/13 (dustin venture builds; re-clones verified green 59/66/38 tests; predicate shipped as scripts/dustin-alpha-omega-done.sh)
review: Root cause of the vanishes is unestablished (no reclaim organ logs a deletion of these paths; scripts/reclaim-worktrees.py sweeps only registered limen worktrees). Diagnosis is deliberately NOT a precondition of the rule: the rule is cheap, the failure is silent, and the durable copy makes the root cause moot for safety. If a future session catches the deleter in the act, extend this precedent rather than minting a duplicate.

subject: Calling EnterWorktree (or otherwise switching a session's isolation root) while subagents are running severs every in-flight agent's Bash rail, unrecoverably. Measured 2026-08-13: three read-only exploration agents were launched from the shared checkout; the parent then entered a worktree to unblock a plan-file write; each agent's next Bash call — including a bare `echo probe` — was refused with 'this command's working directory resolved to the shared checkout', while EnterWorktree from inside the agent refused in the opposite direction ('the current working directory is the repository root, not an isolated worktree'). The two guards form a deadlock the agent cannot exit; Read keeps working (it is cwd-independent), so the agents limp home with partial, read-only results and the missing halves have to be re-run by fresh agents that inherit the worktree cwd. One inventory agent lost its entire gh/git sweep to this.
action: standing rule: isolate FIRST, fan out SECOND. Two bindings. (1) In any session that might write (which a background session must assume — the isolation guard enforced by scripts/hooks/worktree-commit-guard.sh will demand a worktree at the first edit), call EnterWorktree BEFORE launching the first subagent, so every child inherits the worktree cwd from birth. (2) Never call EnterWorktree or ExitWorktree while any subagent or background task is live; if isolation must change, drain the fleet first and relaunch after the switch. Corollary for the children: a subagent that hits the deadlock should stop burning calls on Bash retries and return its Read-only findings with the block named.
authorised_by: session 2026-08-13 (dustin alpha→omega roadmaps; three degraded exploration agents, one fully re-run inventory)
review: Distinct from the reclaim-sweep hazards (scripts/reclaim-worktrees.py) — nothing was deleted here; the agents' processes survived with a dead effector rail. The deadlock is a composition of two individually-correct guards, so the fix is sequencing discipline in the conductor, not a change to either guard.

subject: A session asserted 'person-records stay off GitHub by design' and treated a private store as legitimately local-only. Before asserting any storage/privacy policy, query those owners (or arca.sh status --strict --json for live coverage); a memory line is a hypothesis about them, not a substitute. Corollary: a new private record store is created as ~/Workspace/_<name>-private and NOTHING else — the glob covers it next beat; building any parallel channel violates the single-escrow design (L-ARCA-KEY-ESCROW).

subject: Two sources that LOOK independent often read the same backing store, and querying both then scoring agreement as corroboration is a false-confidence trap. Measured 2026-08-07 (routine-freshness 409 incident): tasks.yaml and `limen status` were both consulted for whether an escalation atom existed, both said no, and the two answers were counted as independent confirmation — but both read the same stale local projection, which lags the conduct keeper. The keeper's 409 'already exists' on the create attempt proved the atom was homed all along; the crash it caused ran for days at severity:silent.
action: standing rule binding CLAUDE.md § Data Grounding: before scoring two readings as corroboration, name each one's backing store; if they share one, it is ONE reading taken twice. For board state specifically, the projection (tasks.yaml and everything derived from it) is a single store — independent confirmation means the keeper itself (the conduct broker) or GitHub, never a second view of the projection.

subject: A predicate that can only pass has no discriminating power, and two shapes produce exactly that: (1) asking a tool a question whose answer is the same whether or not the world is healthy — verify-hot-cache R4 shipped asking `mise current`, which resolves config text and answers identically with the whole toolchain absent from disk (python, node, and uv were all missing while the rung printed green); (2) gating on the exit code of a tool that always exits 0 and carries its verdict in OUTPUT — `mise ls --missing` prints the missing tools and exits 0 either way, so a $?-gate reads green precisely when things are broken.
action: standing rule for every new gate/rung/sensor: before shipping, prove the red path once — fabricate the broken state (or a fixture of it) and watch the predicate actually go red. When a tool inverts the exit-code contract (report-style tools that always exit 0), the gate must parse output emptiness/content, never $?. The fixed rung and its rationale live in scripts/verify-hot-cache.sh R4 comments; this precedent generalizes them to all predicate authorship.
authorised_by: lesson-harvest tranche 2 (session 1f070177, 2026-08-07); fix verified live in scripts/verify-hot-cache.sh
review: empirical close = no new gate ships whose red path was never demonstrated; complements CLAUDE.md 'read the predicate's OWN exit code' (that rule trusts exit codes over pipelines; this one says know when the exit code carries no verdict at all)

subject: Sealing a manifest by exact head OID against a ledger that refreshes on a clock interval is unsatisfiable in a live estate: pr-lifecycle-estate-manifest.py aborted on first divergence (BLOCKED) twice in a row because its census ledger refreshed every ≤20h while the estate absorbed hundreds of dependabot PRs and a sibling background job labeled 249 of its 278 items mid-window. No zero-drift window ever existed, so the manifest could never apply.
action: standing rule: pin-by-OID is for dead targets (a merged SHA, a sealed archive). For a live estate, an apply step must tolerate benign drift — re-derive per item at effect time and treat already-done as success (the shape pr-lifecycle-autotype.py uses: re-check each candidate at effect time via gh pr view; closed/already-labeled = skip, not abort). A designer proposing an exact-state seal over data with its own refresh clock must show the zero-drift window exists before building.

subject: Session-noise Rule 1 ('repair auth, don't disable the capability') has a verified exception: when a capability is doctrinally rejected in the registries (stripe: rejected in pillars.yaml and moneta's design — no processor in the path) and already disabled in sibling lanes, disabling it in the remaining lane is cross-lane PARITY, not silencing a symptom. subject: A retry loop whose exit condition depends on a cross-process contract that is assumed rather than asserted can be structurally unable to terminate. Measured 2026-08-04→05: a 27.5-hour retry loop waited for 'daily-execute stops saying blocked', but the confirmation counter read receipts filtered by run_id while the receipt writer, invoked out-of-band, wrote under a different run_id namespace — success was impossible by construction, and every stage's returncode 0 kept the loop looking healthy while run.status stayed blocked the whole time.
action: standing rule: before arming any retry/poll loop, (1) assert the contract the exit condition depends on — prove one success round-trip (the receipt the writer writes IS the receipt the reader reads, same key/namespace) before looping; (2) bound the loop with a hard deadline and a loud TIMEOUT verdict (the shape scripts/await-pr.sh ships); (3) never read process exit codes as pipeline verdicts — application status is a separate axis (memory limen-gate-gotchas item 16). An unbounded loop with an unasserted contract is the endless-watcher ban's generalization beyond PR gates.
authorised_by: lesson-harvest tranche 3 (session da42bdb7, 2026-08-06); receipt-fabrication fix verified landed per session record
review: empirical close = no future loop runs >deadline on a contract never proven once

subject: A probe whose fixture dies before measurement is indistinguishable, in its own output, from a probe whose measuring API does not work. Measured 2026-08-15: an exec-identity probe built its fixture by copying /bin/sleep and /bin/echo. Those are Apple platform binaries (codesign: Platform identifier=26) carrying a launch constraint pinning them to their canonical path, so the kernel SIGKILLed every copy at exec (EXC_CRASH, Namespace CODESIGNING Code 4, Launch Constraint Violation). proc_pidpath returned None and ps -o comm= returned <defunct>; three consecutive re-runs (three crash reports, 11:56/11:58/12:00) each blamed ctypes/proc_pidpath 'not binding' and the actual question went unanswered. A second defect in the same probe linked every arm to one inode, so proc_pidpath's name-cache resolution reported an arbitrary alias and all arms agreed with each other while measuring nothing.
action: standing rule: a probe must assert its fixture behaved before reading anything from it, and a fixture failure must raise loudly rather than return a datum (the shape scripts/probe-exec-identity.py ships: launch child, assert proc.poll() is None, else raise FixtureError). Two macOS-specific corollaries: never build a fixture from a copy of an Apple binary (use a locally compiled adhoc binary; a SYMLINK to a platform binary survives, a COPY does not), and never share an inode across arms of a path-identity probe. Generalizes the Data Grounding rule that 'I found nothing' and 'I read nothing' are indistinguishable in the output, from corpus retrieval to instrumentation.
authorised_by: session bd5fddec (2026-08-15); fixture A/B verified (copy exit 137, compiled exit 0) and the corrected probe merged as limen#2457
review: empirical close = no future probe in this estate reports an inconclusive measurement that a liveness assertion would have caught

subject: A predicate built to guard a finding can be structurally unable to detect the change it exists to watch for, if its comparison is made against a quantity the finding does not actually depend on. Measured 2026-08-15: scripts/tcc-identity-attribution-probe.py refuted the symlink cure for the rotating per-version TCC identity (#1703) by comparing `ps -p <pid> -o comm=` against the symlink's own path. That is the kernel's ACCOUNTING STRING (p_comm), not the code identity a TCC client derives from — and it holds regardless of what the deciding layer does, so the ratchet would have read OK forever in either world. The deciding layer says the opposite: a platform binary's launch constraint is VIOLATED by a copy at a temp path (SIGKILL) but SATISFIED by a symlink at that same path, which is possible only if the kernel resolved the link before judging the binary. The probe's own output already carried the disconfirming evidence (its symlink child ran to completion rather than reporting <defunct>) and was read past.
action: standing rule: when writing a predicate that ratchets a finding, name the layer the finding depends on and measure THAT layer; then ask the falsification question — 'if the world flipped, would this comparison change?' If not, the predicate is decoration and must be rewritten or marked unresolved. Prefer a discriminator whose outcome the system decides and is binary (a process lives or is killed) over a string the prober chooses to read. Corollary for reviewers: a probe's raw output can contain the evidence that refutes its own verdict — read the observations, not only the verdict line.
authorised_by: session bd5fddec (2026-08-15); amended in limen#2457, which rewrote the cure-B arm to watch code identity and wired the ratchet to the beat (sensors.yaml 0g8b)
review: empirical close = no future ratchet in this estate passes on a comparison that is invariant to the state it claims to guard
